FINAL EXPERIMENT DESIGN (design-only; nothing executed, no results fabricated)

1. OBJECTIVE AND PRIMARY PASS/FAIL CRITERION (up front)
Question: Do sampled trajectories from the forward simulation model show distributional similarity to ground-truth MD trajectories across backbone torsions, sidechain torsions, and top TICA components for all-atom tetrapeptide MD (per neurips2024/93022/0:setup_2)?
Primary prespecified criterion: For each CV, compute squared MMD (unbiased estimator, RBF kernel) between held-out reference frames and sampled frames with a permutation test (999 permutations). A CV family PASSES if for every CV in the family: (a) BH-corrected (FDR q=0.05) permutation p > 0.05, AND (b) observed MMD^2 does not exceed tau = 2 x (95th percentile of the reference-vs-reference split-half null MMD^2 for that CV). The split-half null is the noise floor of genuine MD finite-sample variation; the 2x margin makes tau conservative. Each comparison is accompanied by a trajectory-level block-bootstrap 95% CI (1000 resamples) on the effect size; the claim requires the CI lower bound below tau. Family-level verdicts (backbone / sidechain / TICA) are reported; the overall answer is their conjunction. Rationale: with ~10^4-frame equalized samples, permutation p-values alone are near-ubiquitously significant, so the noise-floor-calibrated effect-size threshold is the decision-relevant quantity.

2. DATA AND DOCUMENTED ASSUMPTIONS
Fixed requirements: all-atom tetrapeptide MD system; backbone AND sidechain torsions both in the CV set; top TICA components included; the specified controls and sensitivities; design-only.
Documented assumptions: A1 ground truth = the paper's tetrapeptide MD dataset, assumed ~10^5-10^6 aggregate frames (only >=2x10^5 needed; smaller data shrinks subsample to 5x10^3 and recalibrates tau). A2 samples produced by the provided forward-model checkpoint under the source sampling regime (assumed autoregressive); no frame-level pairing required. A3 sampled frame count chosen to match 10^4 reference evaluation frames (or reference subsampled to match). A4 TICA software = deeptime, with PyEMMA or a ~50-line NumPy direct implementation as documented fallback (TICA on a ~34-dim feature space is a small generalized eigenproblem). A5 CPU-only budget; all statistics designed to finish in <1 CPU-hour.

3. CONCRETE CV SET FOR A TETRAPEPTIDE
Backbone: phi_i for i=2,3,4 (phi_1 undefined without preceding C'), psi_i for i=1,2,3 (psi_4 included only if C-terminus is capped, noted), omega_i for i=1,2,3 (kept; trans/cis population is a meaningful cheap check) = 9 torsions. Sidechain: chi_1 for every residue except Gly/Ala (up to 4), chi_2 for residues with a second heavy-atom torsion (Asp/Asn/Glu/Gln/His/Phe/Tyr/Trp/Leu/Ile/Met/Lys/Arg; up to 3-4) = typically 5-8 torsions; sparse-occupancy torsions are reported, not dropped. All torsions encoded as (sin, cos). TICA: fitted on all sin/cos dihedral features (~28-34 dims); PRIMARY = top 4 components (rationale: tetrapeptide conformational space has a handful of metastable basins set by phi/psi; 4 components capture dominant slow modes and remain interpretable), n=2 carried in sensitivity. Total CV set ~18-21 CVs.

4. TICA PROTOCOL
Features: sin/cos of all torsions, mean-free. Fit on calibration split only. Lag from {1,5,10,20,50} x frame spacing selected by VAMP-2 score on the held-out evaluation split. Top 4 eigenvectors frozen; sampled trajectories are projected through the frozen transform (never refit on samples). Sanity gate: split-half eigenvector cosine similarity >= 0.99 for top 4, else TICA-CV conclusions are blocked.

5. SPLITS AND COMPARISON SETS
Trajectory-level split of ground truth: 50% calibration / 50% held-out evaluation. Calibration used for TICA fit, MMD bandwidth (median heuristic), bin edges, and the split-half null (calibration half A vs half B, identical pipeline, same 10^4-frame subsampling). Samples never touch calibration. Evaluation reference (10^4 frames) vs samples (10^4 frames) is the headline comparison.

6. METRICS
Backbone and sidechain families: primary MMD^2 + permutation test on standardized sin/cos features; secondary circular Wasserstein-1, KS on sin/cos, chi rotamer population total-variation distance (sidechains). TICA family: joint MMD^2 on the 4-dim TICA space plus per-component marginals; free-energy profiles F=-kBT ln(p+eps) along IC1-IC4 from 50-bin histograms over the 2nd-98th reference percentile support, RMSE in kJ/mol over bins where both p>10^-3, with per-bin bootstrap CIs. One omnibus MMD^2 over the concatenated feature vector guards against per-CV masking.

7. PROTOCOL (numbered)
(1) Load MD, extract torsions, geometry sanity check. (2) Trajectory-level calibration/evaluation split. (3) Split-half null -> per-CV tau. (4) Generate samples with the forward model (or load pre-generated). (5) Extract identical CVs; frozen TICA projection. (6) Subsample both to 10^4 frames. (7) All metrics + permutation tests + block-bootstrap CIs; BH within family. (8) Apply primary criterion. (9) Controls; headline comparison interpreted only if controls behave as specified. (10) Sensitivity analyses; verdicts called robust only if unchanged across settings.

8. CONTROLS
Positive: evaluation-style comparison of calibration half A vs half B (must pass; establishes noise floor and pipeline correctness). Negative: (a) samples vs time-shuffled reference (destroys kinetics while roughly preserving marginals — specifically stresses the kinetic TICA family); (b) samples vs reference with CVs perturbed by Gaussian noise of ~1 rotamer width (must fail; if not, the criterion is insensitive and the design is revised before conclusions). Leakage control: re-run headline comparison with TICA refit on the evaluation split; qualitative agreement reported as robustness note.

9. SENSITIVITY ANALYSES
TICA lag {1,5,10,20,50}x frame spacing; n_components {2,4}; MMD bandwidth {0.5x,1x,2x} median heuristic; bins {25,50,100}; subsample {5x10^3,10^4}.

10. FEASIBILITY
CV extraction for ~10^6 frames: minutes. TICA on ~34 dims: trivial. Dominant cost is MMD with n=10^4/set: full kernel blocks (10^8 entries) computed once in chunked float32 cross-block form; all 999 permutations reuse index-shuffled blocks; minutes-to-tens-of-minutes per CV, <1 CPU-hour total across ~20 CVs on the 224-core CPU budget; no GPU. Software is feasible offline even without packages (direct NumPy implementations of dihedrals and TICA). Data requirement (>=2x10^5 reference frames, >=10^4 sampled frames) is modest for any tetrapeptide MD dataset.

11. LIMITATIONS
CAN claim: statistical indistinguishability, at the prespecified effect-size resolution, of the distributions of backbone torsions, sidechain torsions/rotamers, top TICA components, and free-energy profiles along those components. CANNOT claim: (i) kinetic correctness (TICA projections compared marginally do not verify transition rates/implied timescales; an optional non-decision implied-timescale check could be added); (ii) completeness beyond the chosen CVs (no distances, contacts, RMSD, solvent); (iii) frame- or path-level fidelity for autoregressive sampling; (iv) out-of-distribution generalization to novel sequences; (v) with equalized samples, "no detectable difference" is a statement about tau, not proof of identity — the bootstrap-CI requirement mitigates but does not eliminate low-power false passes, and correlation effects are handled approximately via trajectory-level block bootstrap and effective-sample-size reporting; (vi) dataset-dependent assumptions A1-A5 are documented, not verified, in this design-only deliverable and must be confirmed at execution against the dataset card and the source setup topics.

**Primary criterion (prespecified):** For each collective variable (CV) in each of the three families (backbone torsions, sidechain torsions, top TICA components), compute the squared maximum mean discrepancy (MMD²) between held-out reference MD frames and sampled frames, with a permutation test (999 permutations). Backbone torsions: φ (C'-N-CA-C) defined for residues 2–4 (residue 1 φ often undefined/ill-defined without cap; actually φ of first residue involves N-H... φ1 uses preceding C' which doesn't exist; typically report φ for residues 2–4 and ψ for residues 1–3). Ω (omega, CA-C-N-CA) for residues 1–3 (peptide bonds). Also terminal ψ4 and φ1 may be excluded. So: φ2,φ3,φ4; ψ1,ψ2,ψ3; ω1,ω2,ω3 → 9 backbone torsions (8 if ω dropped; keep ω as it's cheap). Sidechain χ1 for each residue whose sidechain has χ (i.e., not Gly/Ala; Ala has no χ1), χ2 for residues with two heavy-atom sidechain torsions (Asp, Asn, Glu, Gln, His, Phe, Tyr, Trp, Leu, Met, Lys, Arg). Count depends on sequence; state formula and example: worst case ~4 χ1 + 3-4 χ2 ≈ 7-8 sidechain torsions. Total CV dimension ~16-17 torsions → sin/cos encoding → ~32-34 features, well within TICA feasibility.

TICA: features = all sin/cos dihedral features (dimension ~34), lag time candidates {1, 5, 10, 20, 50 frames} chosen by VAMP-2 score on calibration set; top 4 components reported (2 as sensitivity). Software: deeptime (or PyEMMA); assume deeptime available, fallback manual implementation — note as assumption.

- Marginal per-torsion: Wasserstein-1 on circular data (use circular Wasserstein or on sin/cos), KS on sin/cos components.
- Joint MMD: RBF kernel on standardized sin/cos features, bandwidth median heuristic on calibration set; unbiased MMD² estimator; permutation test 999 permutations; subsample 10^4 per set.
- Energy distance: alternative if MMD too heavy; energy distance is O(n²) too. Fine.
- Free-energy profiles along TICA IC1..IC4: 50-bin histograms over shared range (2nd–98th percentile of reference), F = -kBT ln(p+ε), RMSE over bins where both p > threshold; also per-bin bootstrap CI.
